{{For|the American microbiologist (1930–2005)|Milton P. Gordon}}

'''Milton Andrew Gordon''' (May 25, 1935 – April 18, 2017) was an American mathematician and academic administrator. He served as the fourth president of [[California State University, Fullerton]] from 1990 to 2012, making him the fourth African American president in the [[California State University]] system. During his presidency, Cal State Fullerton grew substantially in enrollment and campus facilities. Before joining Cal State Fullerton, Gordon held faculty and administrative positions at [[Chicago State University]] and [[Sonoma State University]].<ref name=Xia>{{cite news |last=Xia |first=Rosanna |title=Milton A. Gordon Dies at 81; Former Cal State Fullerton President Oversaw Era of Increased Diversity and Growth |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |date=19 April 2017 |url=https://www.latimes.com/local/lanow/la-me-20170419-milton-gordon-cal-state-fullerton-20170419-story.html |access-date=13 July 2026}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Milton Andrew Gordon was born on May 25, 1935, in [[Chicago, Illinois]]. His father was from the segregated South in Louisiana but had moved to Chicago to make a better home for his family.<ref>{{cite news |title=Campus and Community Join to Celebrate the Life of CSUF President Milton A. Gordon |newspaper=Los Angeles Sentinel |date=19 October 2017 |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1963838187 |via=ProQuest}}</ref> He earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics and secondary education from [[Xavier University of Louisiana]]. Later he received a master's degree in mathematics from the [[University of Detroit]] and a doctorate in mathematics from the [[Illinois Institute of Technology]].<ref name=Xia />

==Career==
Gordon began his career as an elementary school teacher in the [[Chicago Public Schools]]. Later he worked as a mathematics instructor at the Illinois Institute of Technology and served as director of the Afro-American Studies Program at [[Loyola University Chicago]].<ref name=Xia /><ref name=HACU>{{cite web |title=Milton Gordon, Ph.D. |website=HACU Hall of Champions |publisher=Hispanic Association of Colleges and Universities |date=2017 |url=https://hacu.net/hall_of_champions/dr-milton-a-gordon/ |access-date=13 July 2026}}</ref> 

He was also professor of mathematics and dean of the College of Arts and Sciences at [[Chicago State University]].<ref name=Xia /><ref name=HACU /> 

In 1986 he became vice president for academic affairs and professor of mathematics at [[Sonoma State University]]. He was appointed the fourth president of [[California State University, Fullerton]], in August 1990,<ref>{{cite news |title=Mathematician, 54, Named President of Cal State Fullerton |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |date=16 May 1990 |pages=15 |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/281163744 |via=ProQuest}}</ref> and served as president until 2012.<ref name=Xia /><ref name=HACU />    
 
Gordon was the fourth African American president in the [[California State University]] system. He was also the first Black president at a predominately white university to succeed another Black president.<ref>{{cite news |last=Lindgren |first=Kristina |title=Changes at CSUF Include a Tall Man: University: A New President, a Campus Building Boom, Higher Gas Prices and Higher Tuition Await Students |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |date=3 September 1990 |pages=1 |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/281282247 |via=ProQuest}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Lindgren |first=Kristina |title=University's New President Warns of Cuts |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |date=31 August 1990 |pages=7 |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/281065212 |via=ProQuest}}</ref> He led CSUF during a period of enrollment growth from about 25,700 to more than 36,000 students. He oversaw the addition of 13 academic degree programs, including a doctorate in education. During his presidency, CSUF undertook more than $636 million in campus construction, including the expansion of the Pollak Library and the construction of the Mihaylo College of Business and Economics. He supported the opening of satellite campuses in [[Santa Ana, California|Santa Ana]] and [[Garden Grove, California|Garden Grove]], as well as the establishment of a branch campus in [[Mission Viejo]], later relocated to [[Irvine, California|Irvine]]. He served as president during a period in which Cal State Fullerton became the leading California university in graduating Latino students.<ref name=Xia />  

Soon after Gordon became president, the California State University system faced a severe budget crisis involving planned layoffs and program closures.<ref>{{cite news |last=Lindgren |first=Kristina |title=Cal State Faces Slash 'Almost Triple' 1990's: Education: Fullerton Campus Must Trim at Least $14 Million, the University President Says. Staffing, Enrollment, Materials and Academic Programs May Be Affected, Along with Football |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |date=27 January 1991 |pages=1 |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/281288937 |via=ProQuest}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Gordon |first=Larry |title=CSU Plans to Lay Off 2,200 Unless State Helps Education: Chancellor Says Tenured Faculty, Staff Will Lose Jobs if Funds Are Not Provided. He Calls for Tuition Hike, Early Retirement and Capping Budget Cuts at 6% |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |date=6 June 1992 |pages=1 |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/281700375 |via=ProQuest}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Lindgren |first=Kristina |title=Class Struggles: Budget Worries, Cutbacks Cloud Fall Semester at Cal State Fullerton |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |date=30 August 1992 |pages=1 |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/281788458 |via=ProQuest}}</ref> Subsequent state funding changes reduced the extent of the projected cuts.<ref>{{cite news |last=Cummer |first=Willson |title=Fullerton Cal State Cuts Not as Bad as Feared |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |date=30 October 1992 |pages=3 |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/281729270 |via=ProQuest}}</ref> Nevertheless, the [[Cal State Fullerton Titans football|CSUF football program]] was discontinued in 1992 during the budget crisis.<ref>{{cite news |last=DiGiovanna |first=Mike |title=CS Fullerton to Drop Football; Costs Cited: Economics: School President Says Move to Less-Expensive Division I-AA Is Planned for 1994 |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |date=8 December 1992 |pages=1 |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/281986915 |via=ProQuest}}</ref>

During Gordon's presidency, CSUF was the subject of several state audits that identified weaknesses in financial management and internal controls. A 1999 investigation by the [[California State Auditor]] concluded that the university had engaged in serious financial mismanagement, citing the misuse of donated and scholarship funds for expenditures such as meals, entertainment, gifts, vehicle maintenance, and other non-educational purposes. The audit also found that university officials had bypassed competitive hiring and contracting procedures, improperly transferred funds to a university foundation, and failed to comply with restrictions governing charitable donations and scholarship accounts. Chancellor [[Charles B. Reed]] and Gordon acknowledged errors in judgment but disputed the characterization of the findings as serious mismanagement and instituted reviews of campus business practices. A subsequent state audit released in 2006 found that, between 2001 and 2004, the university continued to experience waste, poor record-keeping, inadequate oversight, conflicts of interest in contracting, and weaknesses in financial controls, while some employees reported fearing retaliation for reporting misconduct. Gordon stated that he had begun implementing reforms after learning of the problems in 2003, increased financial oversight, and that several employees left the university following the investigation.<ref>{{cite news |last=Gottlieb |first=Jeff |title=Audit Rips Cal State Fullerton; Scholarship Money Was Spent on Meals and Carwashes, Say Investigators. Nothing Serious, Says University |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |date=15 December 1999 |pages=1 |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/421468120 |via=ProQuest}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Mehta |first=Seema |title=Cal State Fullerton Audit Shows Past Fiscal Abuse |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |date=27 October 2006 |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/422078476 |via=ProQuest}}</ref>

During his tenure at CSUF, Gordon held leadership positions with several professional organizations including the [[Hispanic Association of Colleges and Universities]] and the [[American Council on Education]].<ref name=Xia /> Iin 2019, CSUF's University Hall was renamed Milton A. Gordon Hall to recognize his accomplishments.<ref>{{cite news |title=Cal State Fullerton’s Hall Renamed to Honor Former President Milton A. Gordon |newspaper=Los Angeles Sentinel |date=25 January 2019 |url=https://lasentinel.net/cal-state-fullertons-hall-renamed-to-honor-former-president-milton-a-gordon.html |access-date=13 July 2026}}</ref>

==Honors and awards==
* 2011 – Professional Achievement Award, ([[Illinois Institute of Technology]])<ref name=HACU />
* 2010 – President's Award of Excellence, ([[Hispanic Association of Colleges and Universities]])<ref name=HACU />
* 2010 – Alfredo G. de los Santos Jr. Distinguished Leadership in Higher Education Award, ([[American Association of Hispanics in Higher Education]] )<ref name=HACU />
* 2010 – Man of the Year Award, presented jointly by Christ Our Redeemer AME Church, the Black Chamber of Orange County, 100 Black Men of Orange County, and the Orange County Ministerial Alliance.<ref name=HACU />

==Personal life and death==
Gordon married Margaret Faulwell in 1987.<ref>{{cite news |last=Conway |first=Ann |title=In Home; Cal State Fullerton; The Official Home of the Campus President Is a Peaceful, Unpretentious Mansion. Living There, Though, Has Its Challenges, Milton Gordon Says |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |date=3 March 2001 |pages=N1 |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/421610472 |via=ProQuest}}</ref> He had three sons. He died on April 18, 2017, at the age of 81.<ref name=Xia />
